test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 19 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements about conductivity of electricity in ionic compounds is correct?

options.text: Ionic compounds are bad conductors of electricity in both solid as well as in molten state.
Ionic compounds conduct electricity in solid state but not in molten state.
Ionic compounds conduct electricity in molten state but not in solid state.
Ionic compounds conduct electricity in both solid as well as in molten state.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ionic compounds conduct electricity in molten state but not in solid state.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Ionic compounds conduct electricity in molten state but not in solid state because in molten state their ions are free to move from place to place.
 
• ionic compounds cannot conduct electricity in solid state because their ions are fixed together and cannot move.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Ions of opposite charges are tightly packed together to create crystalline solids known as ionic compounds.
 
• Ionic compounds often result from reactions between metals and non-metals.
